newsitem.title: CHINA: China says needs oil, gas shareholding reform.
newsitem.headline: China says needs oil, gas shareholding reform.

text.p: China should expand shareholding reforms in its oil and natural gas sector and more listed firms were needed, an official of the China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) said on Monday.
Shareholding reform was the key to boosting profits, said the official, who asked not to be identified.
Three oil and gas firms under CNPC have been listed so far -- Shengli Daming, Jinan Diesel, and Long Champ, the official said.
Another company, Liaohe Jinma Oilfield Co, will list 200 million A shares for domestic investors in near future, he said.
China also has listed a number of oil-related companies that are under the direction of the nation's state refiner, Sinopec, as well as firms in the petrochemical business.
Beijing has recently been pushing for faster reform of its inefficient state enterprises and the listing of shares appears to be one of the areas where new steps will be taken.

CNPC would encourage more firms to carry on shareholding reforms, so that they could become more efficient, the official said without identifying any of the companies or giving any timetables for the plans.
He said , however, that these companies face problems such as varying standards for the assessment of fixed assets and calculations of oil reserves, he said.
